data.name: Majnu
data.gender_notes: Majnu is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is mad with love for a beloved, often referring to the character Majnun Rumi in Persian mythology. The name Majnu carries the meaning “Mad with love” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Majnu usually hope their child will grow to embody mad with love and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of deep, selfless love and devotion.
data.etymology: Majnu belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mad with love.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Majnu total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Majnu holds significant cultural impact within the Hindu and Islamic communities, mainly due to the legendary Persian poet Rumi, whose life story is rooted in the theme of divine, intense love. In Hindu literature too, one finds this name attributed to characters who were known for their dedication and love towards their beloved. The essence of the name resonates across borders and transcends religious affiliations, reflecting the power and enduring nature of love.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Majnu lies in its association with selfless and unwavering love for the divine or one's beloved. The name invokes images of the Sufi mystic Rumi, who embodies the essence of spiritual love with his poetic works. Through his life and literature, Rumi expresses the idea that love for the divine is the ultimate goal, and one should surrender oneself completely to this love, freeing the soul and guiding it towards enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Majnu is a name of divine madness in love, inspired by the legendary figure of the same name from Indian folklore. It represents an intense longing and devotion, transcending rational thought and societal norms. In essence, it symbolizes the ecstatic union with the beloved, be it a deity or a mortal, merging the individual self in the infinite divine love.
